text: Given the server is running, When a client calls tools/list, Then the 9 new tools (rootly_postmortems_list/get/update, rootly_action_items_list/get/create/update, rootly_oncalls_list, rootly_schedules_override_create) are listed with their documented required parameters

Given an incident retrospective still in draft status and never opened in Rootly's collaborative editor, When rootly_postmortems_update is called with a new title and content, Then the call succeeds and a following rootly_postmortems_get shows the new values
steps: Pick a Rootly incident whose post-mortem is draft and has never been opened in the web retrospective editor

Call rootly_postmortems_update(postmortem_id, title="", content="

new content

")
expect: update call returns the resource with the new title/content; the following get call shows the same new title/content
notes: needs a real vendor account; not run at design time

text: Given a retrospective already opened in Rootly's collaborative editor, When rootly_postmortems_update is called with new content, Then the tool returns a structured, non-crashing error naming the conflict instead of raising an exception
steps: Open an incident's retrospective in Rootly's web collaborative editor at least once
expect: the tool returns a JSON error envelope ({"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "retryable": ...}}), not a stack trace or empty response
notes: needs a real vendor account; not run at design time

text: Given a post-mortem id that does not exist, When rootly_postmortems_get or rootly_postmortems_update is called, Then the tool returns the existing not_found error envelope
Given an incident id, When rootly_action_items_create is called with a summary, Then Rootly creates the action item under that incident and the tool returns its id and status
steps: Pick a real Rootly incident id
Call rootly_action_items_create(incident_id, summary="Add a dashboard alert for X")
Open the incident in Rootly's UI, or call rootly_action_items_list(incident_id)
expect: the create call returns an id and status=open; the action item is visible under the incident in Rootly
notes: needs a real vendor account; not run at design time

text: Given action items exist across the org, When rootly_action_items_list is called with no incident_id and a status or priority filter, Then only matching items are returned, paginated like every other list tool (items/count/total/page/has_more, offset/next_offset)
steps: Ensure the org has action items in more than one status
expect: each call returns only action items matching the given filter; the response includes count/total/page/has_more and, if has_more is true, next_offset
notes: needs a real vendor account; the pagination mechanics themselves (offset math, cut-page walking) are covered by TC-paging-auto below, not this manual case

text: rootly_postmortems_list pagination (offset math, cut-page walking, has_more) matches every other list tool in this server
rootly_action_items_list (org-wide mode) pagination matches every other list tool in this server

Given incident_id is passed to rootly_action_items_list together with status/priority/kind, When called, Then the tool raises a clear invalid_argument error instead of silently ignoring the unsupported filter
Given an open action item, When rootly_action_items_update is called with status=done, Then Rootly marks it done and the tool returns the updated record
steps: Pick a real action item with status open
notes: needs a real vendor account; not run at design time

text: Given no schedule filter, When rootly_oncalls_list is called, Then it returns who is on call right now, grouped by escalation policy, using the same flattened JSON shape as every other resource
steps: Identify a schedule with a known current on-call user
expect: the known on-call user's id appears in the result, with schedule_id/schedule_name/escalation_policy_* fields flattened the same way other tools flatten JSON:API resources
notes: needs a real vendor account; not run at design time

text: Given a schedule id, a user id and a start/end time, When rootly_schedules_override_create is called, Then Rootly reassigns on-call coverage for that window, and calling it again with the same user and times returns the existing override rather than creating a duplicate
steps: Call rootly_schedules_override_create(schedule_id, user_id, starts_at, ends_at) for a future window
Confirm in Rootly's UI (or rootly_oncalls_list during that window) that the user is now on call
Call rootly_schedules_override_create again with the identical schedule_id/user_id/starts_at/ends_at
expect: first call creates the override (201) and coverage changes for that window; second identical call returns the same override id (200), not a new one
notes: needs a real vendor account; not run at design time

text: Given a required field is missing or invalid for a write tool added by this ticket, When it is called, Then the existing invalid_argument error envelope is returned, not an unhandled exception
Given no X-Rootly-Api-Token header, When any of the 9 new tools is called, Then the gateway middleware returns 401 before the tool body runs
notes: extend the parametrization/coverage of these two existing tests to include the 9 new tool names, same shape as the existing tools
